ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo (as amended by Ley 19/2021); Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, por el que se aprueba el Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010; Real Decreto 973/2021, de 9 de noviembre, regulador de la declaración de titularidad real (Registro de Titularidades Reales, RTR); Ley 14/2013 de apoyo a emprendedores; Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC). UBO identification is also integrated through the Registro Mercantil Central and notarial protocols under the framework of Directive (EU) 2015/849 as transposed.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Name Reservation issued by the Registro Mercantil Central (Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Spain is a contracting party to the 1961 Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation (Escritura de Constitución) and statutory articles (Estatutos Sociales)
Certificate of the Registro Mercantil confirming inscription and corporate directorship and UBO registration (Certificación del Registro Mercantil del domicilio social)
Power of Attorney executed by each non-resident shareholder or director for incorporation and banking formalities (Poder de representación)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Spanish Notary or foreign notary subject to apostille
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization if origin is non-Hague party)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO Declaration form (Escritura de titularidad real / declaración del titular real) filed with the Commercial Registry and the Registro de Titularidades Reales
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registro Mercantil Provincial / Registro de Titularidades Reales (RTR)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille on any foreign supporting identification documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport or national identity card of each shareholder and director (PEP and sanction screening package)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Consular office or competent authority of the country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the European Commission’s consolidated list of persons, groups and entities subject to EU financial sanctions; OFAC’s Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN) for USD transactions and any international transfers; UN Security Council Consolidated List; Spanish Ministry of Economy and Digital Transformation’s list of sanctioned persons under Royal Decree 176/2020; and the RTR’s risk-based due diligence protocol. PEP screening is obligatory for all non-resident shareholders and beneficial owners under Article 14 of Ley 10/2010, including verification via approved commercial databases and notarial record of source of funds. Enhanced due diligence is required when the shareholder is domiciled in a high-risk third jurisdiction as per FATF public statements. All screening must be repeated within 30 days before incorporation and again at account opening and on any share transfer.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central – Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social (online via https://www.rmc.es, also functional through Colegio de Registradores de España)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Spanish, or any official language of Spain (Catalan, Basque, Galician, Occitan/Aranese), and are required to use Latin script characters. The name may not include symbols or abbreviations other than S.L., S.L.U., and possibly 'Sociedad Limitada'. For names originating in non-Latin alphabets (e.g., Chinese, Cyrillic, Arabic), a phonetic transliteration into Spanish/Latin script is mandatory and must be certified by a sworn translator. The name must be grammatically distinctive and cannot infringe on prior registered names or trademarks; the Registro Mercantil Central applies a rule of phonetic identity and exact spelling identity for confusion avoidance.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name certification application is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative appeal (recurso de reposición) with the Registro Mercantil Central within one month of the notice of rejection, presenting a reasoned brief and any supporting comparables. If the Registry fails to rectify, the applicant may file a formal complaint (queja) with the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (Ministry of Justice) under the Código de Procedimiento Español de Legalidad Registral. Further appeal is possible before the civil courts (juzgado de lo mercantil) under Article 18 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital. A rejected name request may be resubmitted with a different proposed token, but the same denomination cannot be re-filed unless the grounds of rejection are cured. Extensions of the name reservation window are possible on payment of additional fees, but each certificate is valid for 30 days and may be renewed for up to three consecutive 30-day periods.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A fully virtual office with no physical desk sharing is not generally accepted for initial incorporation of an SL under mandatory requirements in Law 14/2013 and the Ley de Sociedades de Capital. However, Spanish commercial law permits a registered office to be any place within Spanish territory, and 'virtual office' service providers in Spain (including Madrid and Barcelona) are accepted if they provide a physical address with a mailbox and a real reception facility for invoicing and official notifications. For an AI/BPO business engaged solely in data labeling with no public-facing physical presence, a registered agent service with a physical office location and mail forwarding is permissible, but the tax authorities (AEAT) and the Commercial Registry may require proof of commensurate commercial substance, generally the retention of a leased office space or an identifiable workplace for employees/contractors. A phased arrangement using a reputable corporate service provider's physical address is accepted during pre-incorporation and for the first 6 months, after which a physical place of operations must be evidenced.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium – 65% probability of an unannounced inspection by the Registro Mercantil or the Agencia Tributaria (AEAT) within the first 18 months if the registered office is flagged as a virtual shared space and the company’s declared employees are under 5 or local payroll is absent. For standard administrative/BPO businesses with a co-working or dedicated office lease, the risk drops to approximately 20%. Inspections may also be conducted by the Social Security Inspectorate (Inspección de Trabajo y Seguridad Social) to verify physical presence and employment records.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el Texto Refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC): Articles 4 (minimum capital), 20-22 (public deed and commercial registration), 62 (sole administrator) and 102-104 (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada); modified by Ley 18/2022 de Creación y Crecimiento de Empresas; notarial formalities under Ley 6/2014 del Notariado.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (name reservation certificate) and Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office (e.g., Registro Mercantil de Madrid); deed executed before a Spanish Notary for the province of the registered office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (public deed of incorporation incorporating the Estatutos Sociales or Articles of Association).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Default statutory minimum under Article 4 LSC is 3,000 EUR fully subscribed and fully paid-up in cash or kind; alternatively, under Ley 18/2022, capital may be fixed at 1 EUR provided full discharge in cash, mandatory legal reserve until reaching 3,000 EUR, and solvency conditions per Article 4.2 LSC. The paid-up amount must be evidenced by a bank certificate of deposit (certificado bancario de desembolso) issued by a Spanish credit institution; non-cash contributions require an independent expert valuation report under Article 67 LSC.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST: All shares issued in the incorporation deed are subscribed and accepted; the paid-up capital of 3,000 EUR (or 1 EUR under the Crea y Crece regime, subject to the statutory reserve) is acknowledged as fully discharged. SECOND: The registered office for statutory, tax and administrative purposes is fixed at [address], Madrid, within the province of Madrid; relocation within the same municipality is delegated to the administrator. THIRD: [Name] is appointed sole administrator (administrador único), exercising all powers of representation with legal limitation of liability. FOURTH: The administrator is mandated to execute all notarial, registry, tax, labour and banking formalities required for incorporation and registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reservation of the corporate name and obtainment of the negative name certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central via the official online portal (ventanilla única / www.registradores.org) or written application to the Central Commercial Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application with one principal proposed company name and at least one alternative name; the Registry verifies that the denomination is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing Spanish or European company name; upon approval a Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social is issued, valid for three months and renewable once for an additional three months; no apostille or legalization is required for domestic founders.
required_dossiers: Official application form for denomination certification
Copy of national ID or passport of applicant incorporator
Power of attorney if application is filed by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the denomination is denied for similarity or identity, file a fresh application with a distinct alternative denomination; no appeal fee applies and resubmission through the same portal remedies the refusal without re-notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the capital deposit account and certification of paid-up share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution supervised by Banco de España (e.g., bank branch chosen by incorporators for the company's future account).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate account in the name of the future SL; deposit the full subscribed capital in cash or by transfer; request a double certificate of deposit (certificado de desembolso) expressly identifying the future company, the subscribers and the amounts paid; for non-cash contributions, annex the statutory expert valuation report; the certificate must be delivered to the notary in original form.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate (Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social)
Draft Articles of Association and share allocation sheet
Identity documents and tax numbers of all subscribing incorporators
Anti-money-laundering and KYC internal forms of the financial institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries KYC documentation, provide corrected corporate information and proof of legal capacity; in case of refusal, select another supervised credit institution and repeat the deposit; alternatively, the notary may document the capital contribution directly through the deed when a bank certificate cannot be timely obtained.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the public deed of incorporation before a Spanish notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary of the province of the future registered office (Notaría de [Madrid]).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the name certificate, bank capital certificate, draft bylaws, share allocation and identity documents to the notary; the notary reviews legal capacity, reads the deed in Spanish to the incorporators, and executes the Escritura de Constitución; after execution, request the first excerpt (primera copia) and the notary's electronic transmission to the Registry and AEAT; the company is not yet a legal person until registration.
required_dossiers: Original negative name certificate in force
Bank certificate of capital deposit (certificado bancario de desembolso)
Draft Articles of Association/Estatutos Sociales
Valid passports or national IDs of incorporators and the sole administrator
Administrator's acceptance declaration (aceptación del cargo)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies legal or drafting defects, the deed may be corrected by amendment instrument (escritura de subsanación) or restated; the notary is obliged to guide the cure and re-execution occurs immediately without loss of the name certificate validity period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Provisional tax identification and payment of Transfer Tax and Stamp Duty (ITP-AJD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) for the provisional NIF; regional tax authority (Hacienda autonómica) for Modelo 600/601 filing and payment.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of deed execution, file the ITP-AJD self-assessment (Modelo 600/601) corresponding to the incorporation operation using the autonomomic modality applicable to Operaciones Societarias; simultaneously apply for the provisional NIF (CIF provisional) via Modelo 036/037, declaring the economic activity CNAE-2009 8220 / ancillary 63.11; attach the provisional NIF to the Registry application and to all subsequent filings.
required_dossiers: First authorised copy of the public deed of incorporation
Modelo 600 or 601 ITP-AJD self-assessment form
Modelo 036 or 037 census declaration
Identity document and tax number of the sole administrator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Modelo 600 or census declaration is rejected, correct the data electronically and resubmit within the effective filing window; late payment surcharges may be reduced through voluntary regularization (Art. 27 LGT); AEAT queries are resolved by uploading the supporting deed copy and identity documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the incorporation deed in the Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office (Registro Mercantil de Madrid for a Madrid seat).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the first authorised copy of the deed together with the provisional NIF, proof of ITP-AJD payment and the standard presentation form; the registrar performs legal qualification (calificación registral) within the statutory 15-day period; upon inscription the company acquires full legal personality; request a certified statement of registration (certificación registral de inscripción) for use before AEAT, Social Security and municipal authorities.
required_dossiers: First authorised copy of the notarial deed
Provisional NIF certificate issued by AEAT
Proof of payment or exemption of ITP-AJD (Modelo 600/601)
Standard registry submission form (formulario de presentación telemática or paper model)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a defect note (nota de calificación), cure the defects through a supplementary notarial instrument and resubmit; the registry must confirm registration within 15 days of the corrected filing; ultimate remedy is appeal to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública under the Mercantile Registry Regulations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Final registration with AEAT, Social Security employer registration and municipal licensing/declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: AEAT (definitive NIF); Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (employer account); Ayuntamiento of the registered office (activity licence or declaración responsable de apertura).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, submit to AEAT the certified registry registration certificate and obtain the definitive NIF (Modelo 036 modification); register the company as an employer with the Seguridad Social (Modelo TA.6, Código de Cuenta de Cotización); for the physical premises, either file the municipal declaración responsable de inicio de actividad or apply for the municipal activity license if the premises exceed the low-impact thresholds; if required, file the environmental communication with the competent regional body.
required_dossiers: Certified certificate of registration in the Commercial Registry
Modelo 036 for definitive NIF and census variation
Employer registration form TA.6 and workplace declaration (Modelo TA.7 if applicable)
Building ownership or lease contract, occupancy certificate (licencia de primera ocupación)
Fire prevention project and building safety certificate for the premises
Environmental communication form where the municipal regime requires it
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality requires corrections to the declaración responsable, rectify within the administrative suspension period and re-file; if a full licence is needed, the municipal procedure follows Ley 39/2015 and administrative silence may be alleged after the legal deadline; AEAT issues the definitive NIF upon verified registry inscription without further scrutiny; Social Security registration is immediate after submission.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Consejería de Medio Ambiente, Agricultura y Vivienda of the competent Comunidad Autónoma (Dirección General de Calidad y Evaluación Ambiental) and the municipal licensing authority of the registered office (e.g., Dirección General de Licencias del Ayuntamiento de Madrid).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia Urbanística de Actividad / Municipal Activity Licence, or Declaración Responsable de Apertura de Establecimiento where the premises are low-impact and under the thresholds of Ley 12/2012 and the municipal ordinance.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Dirección General de Calidad y Evaluación Ambiental - Consejería de Medio Ambiente of the relevant Comunidad Autónoma, coordinated with the Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – office/back-office BPO service described under ISIC 8220 with no industrial plant; not listed in Annex I or Annex II of Ley 21/2013 de Evaluación Ambiental. Premises under 300 m² with no classified fire load and no hazardous materials require only the municipal declaración responsable; premises above 300 m² or containing significant server clusters are subject to simplified environmental registration (comunicación ambiental or incorporación al registro de actividades).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Domestic-grade wastewater only: compliance with municipal sewer discharge ordinance and RD 606/2003 (pH 6.0-9.5, suspended solids <500 mg/l, BOD5 <300 mg/l); negligible VOC emissions from office activity; waste handling per Ley 7/2022 de Residuos with non-hazardous office waste segregated; electrical and electronic equipment waste (WEEE) disposed through an authorised manager per RD 110/2015; server cooling fluids subject to EU F-Gas Regulation 517/2014; noise at facility boundary not exceeding 55 dB(A) day / 45 dB(A) night per RD 1367/2007.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate per RD 513/2017 (RSCIEI) and Código Técnico de la Edificación DB-SI: fire doors, automatic detection, extinguishers at 15m spacing, emergency lighting and evacuation signage; structural load inspection certificate per CTE for office loading; occupational risk prevention workplace health and safety assessment per Ley 31/1995 de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales and RD 171/2004; low-voltage electrical installation certificate per RD 842/2002; first-aid equipment, workplace signage and emergency plan prepared by the preventive organisation; employer registration with an accredited PRL service where workforce exceeds six employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) - www.agenciatributaria.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident-owned Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL): (1) Obtain an NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero) for the foreign legal representative via the Spanish consulate or the Oficina de Extranjería; (2) Execute the public deed of incorporation before a Spanish notary and file it with the Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil); (3) Apply for the provisional NIF/CIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) of the company by filing Modelo 036 (declaración censal) with AEAT within one month of incorporation; (4) Register the company in the IVA census (Censo de Obligados Tributarios); (5) For a non-resident entity without a permanent establishment that is a direct supplier or service recipient, obtain a NIF-N (entity NIF for non-residents) using Modelo 036/030. The definitive NIF is issued subsequent to the registration of the deed; the SL itself is a resident tax entity always subject to the Impuesto sobre Sociedades.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box regime exists; the SL is statutorily a separate taxable entity subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (IS). Available elections include: (i) optional cash-basis IVA (criterio de caja) for SMEs with annual turnover below EUR 2,000,000; (ii) voluntary enrollment in the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) for electronic VAT reporting; (iii) tax consolidation regime (régimen de grupos fiscales) for groups meeting the 75% ownership threshold under Articles 58-64 Ley del Impuesto sobre Sociedades; (iv) the EU Anti-Tax-Avoidance Directive hybrid mismatch disclosures/modeling elections under Article 15 bis LGT and related IS rules. No US-style classification election is applicable; non-resident shareholders do not alter the Spanish entity-level taxation default.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.territorial_scope_note: The SL is a Spanish resident entity taxed on worldwide income. The reference to 'Territorial_Scope' in the schema is not applicable to Spain; the correct classification is Entity_Level_Taxation on worldwide income, with double tax relief available under the OECD Model Tax Convention network and the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido) - Spanish Value Added Tax under Ley 37/1992
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Spain does not operate a general economic turnover exemption threshold analogous to the UK VAT threshold. Any entity performing taxable economic activities within Spanish territory (peninsula, Balearic Islands) is compulsorily required to register in the IVA census prior to commencing activity, irrespective of projected turnover. A reduced-regime threshold applies only for the special simplified schemes (régimen simplificado), which AI/BPO services are not eligible for; the optional cash-basis IVA regime (criterio de caja) is available for taxpayers with annual turnover below EUR 2,000,000. The SII real-time reporting obligation is mandatory for taxpayers with annual turnover exceeding EUR 6,000,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Under Ley 18/2022 'Crea y Crece', all entrepreneurs and professionals must issue, deliver and receive electronic invoices (Facturae format or equivalent structured/XML format) in their B2B relationships. Mandatory phasing: businesses with annual turnover exceeding EUR 8,000,000 must comply within one year of the enabling regulation; all remaining businesses within two years. Invoice issuance must incorporate the standard Spanish obligatory invoice data fields (Serie, NIF del emisor y receptor, Base Imponible, Tipo impositivo, Cuota). For IVA purposes, all invoice data, including customer VAT identification, must be transmitted to AEAT either through the SII real-time fiscal clearance system (mandatory for turnover > EUR 6,000,000; voluntary for others) or through the annual recapitulative statements (Modelo 347/349 for intra-EU supplies). No physical tax stamp is required on invoices; the fiscal clearance is electronic. SII mandates XML structured transmission (Web Service API at https://www.agenciatributaria.es) to AEAT within 4 calendar days of invoice issuance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For services (including computer vision annotation and RLHF data curation BPO): zero-ratd/outside-scope treatment under Article 69.Uno and Article 70.1.2º LIVA applies where the recipient is a taxable person (empresario o profesional) established in another EU Member State or in a third country, provided the effective use and exploitation of the AI data labeling services occurs outside the Spanish IVA territory. The transaction is then taxed under the reverse-charge mechanism at destination (0% in Spain). For B2C supplies to non-EU customers, the 'use and enjoyment' place-of-supply rules may keep the services within Spanish IVA where the tangible work product (e.g., annotated datasets) is physically deployed in Spain; therefore, the BPO must document end-customer establishment and actual use. For goods exports (not the typical BPO model but applicable to any physical data storage devices containing deliverable datasets), a 0% rate applies under Article 21 LIVA where goods are dispatched outside the EU within 3 months, evidenced by the electronic customs declaration (DEX).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Documento Único Administrativo/DUA - DEX) registered in the aduana with electronic data interchange; required for physical goods dispatching (including GPU servers or data-storage devices) outside the EU
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill in the exporter's name evidencing dispatch to the non-EU customer's location
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT/MT103 evidence of collection of export consideration into a Spanish bank account in the company's name
Service Agreement and Work Order between ES_SL and the foreign client stating the nature of the AI data labeling services, the place of supply, and customer's identity
Proof of customer's foreign taxable-person status (EU VAT registration number validated via VIES, or foreign business registration certificate / TIN from the non-EU jurisdiction)
Signed certificate of service delivery and, where applicable, digital acceptance receipt from the offshore client evidencing that the labeled datasets were used/exploited outside Spain
Internal costing and transfer pricing file if the BPO is performed at arm's length (Chapter IV documentation) supporting the commercial rationale of the export flow
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: False or insufficiently documented zero-rating claims are treated as undue tax advantage. AEAT may lawfully deviate the IVA and impose: (i) the difference between the 21% IVA incorrectly omitted and the 0% claim, as tax debt (cuota); (ii) late-payment interest (interés de demora) calculated from the end of the voluntary payment period of the tax period; (iii) a proportional penalty for tax infractions under Ley 58/2003 General Tributaria Article 191, typically 50% to 100% of the cuota, with reduction to 25%/50% where the adjustment is conformed voluntarily; (iv) where fraudulent intent (ánimo de defraudar) is shown, penalties of up to 150% of the cuota, and criminal referral under Articles 305/305 bis Código Penal for amounts exceeding EUR 120,000; (v) denial of refund or re-credit of IVA previously reclaimed in Modelo 303/390 filings, plus derogation for up to six months to model the correct IVA position. In SII compliance audits, failure to file the export-supporting documentation digitally within four days may additionally trigger an Article 203 LGT penalty of EUR 200 per invoice, and non-cooperation in audit procedures (obstrucción) may attract EUR 600.00 to EUR 6,000.00 penalties. Retrospective clawback is generally possible for up to four years from the invoice issuance date (statute of limitations), extended by the fraud limitation rule to ten years in criminal cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain maintains full capital account convertibility and current account convertibility under EU acquis and Spanish law. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are unrestricted and freely convertible without prior regulatory approval, subject only to standard AML/KYC screening and tax compliance filings with the AEAT.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or forced conversion of export proceeds applies in Spain or the EU. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency accounts and converted at market rates. All export transactions require statistical declaration to the Spanish Customs Agency (AEAT) via the TRACES system; banks may request supporting invoices and contracts for transactions exceeding reporting thresholds.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for offshore digital EMIs via licensed platforms such as Wise and PayPal. Legal constraints include mandatory compliance with Spanish Payment Services Directive (PSD2) requirements, Bank of Spain registration for payment institutions, and full AML/KYC verification of the SL entity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital onboarding and KYC is fully permitted for low-risk SL entities. Directors may complete all identification and verification processes electronically via video calls and qualified electronic signatures; physical presence is not mandated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained source of funds or client payment patterns inconsistent with data-labeling revenue
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed client contracts, detailed service invoices, bank statements proving legitimate revenue from AI annotation and RLHF projects, business incorporation certificate, and shareholder declarations

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections routed via SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' or 'EQUITY INJECTION'. Verification requires Spanish SL incorporation certificate, shareholder agreement, proof of funds source, and beneficial ownership documentation. All wires processed through correspondent banking networks with full AML screening.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements executed via SWIFT MT103 or MT202. Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) available through correspondent banks for international trade. All disbursements supported by trade contracts, invoices, and delivery documents; subject to ongoing AML monitoring and tax reporting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts by the shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company shareholders; no separate filing authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end; normally by 30 June for a 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Corporate governance non-compliance; may delay the Mercantile Registry filing and expose directors to liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholder approval; normally by 31 July for a 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure after one year of non-filing, preventing most subsequent filings; administrative fines generally range from EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000, subject to statutory limits and company size.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership declaration and confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Mercantile Registry and the Central Register of Beneficial Ownership, as applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Beneficial ownership information is generally confirmed with the annual accounts filing; changes must be recorded promptly and generally within two months of becoming known
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry filing defects, possible registry closure, sanctions under Spanish anti-money-laundering legislation, and potential director liability for inaccurate or omitted information.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Legalization of accounting books and corporate books
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Mercantile Registry of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the financial year-end; normally by 30 April for a 31 December year-end, through the electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry processing issues and potential evidentiary and director-liability consequences; late legalization may impair the company's ability to evidence properly maintained books.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the first 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the tax year-end; normally 1 to 25 July for a calendar-year company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties, late-payment interest, tax surcharges, and potential tax audit or assessment; penalties depend on whether tax is payable and whether the filing is voluntary.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is generally required when the company exceeds at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: EUR 4 million total assets, EUR 8 million net annual turnover, or 50 average employees. Mandatory audit also applies to certain regulated or public-interest entities and other cases prescribed by law.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad) and applicable Spanish commercial-accounting legislation. IFRS is generally relevant for consolidated accounts of listed groups and may apply in other legally permitted or required circumstances.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must identify and maintain current information on its ultimate beneficial owners. The beneficial ownership declaration is generally confirmed or updated in connection with the annual accounts filing. Changes in ownership or control must be reflected in the Register of Members and reported through the applicable Mercantile Registry or beneficial ownership mechanism within the prescribed period. Share transfers are not replaced by an annual confirmation and must be documented and entered in the Register of Members.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Sole Shareholder, if applicable
Register of Contracts with the Sole Shareholder, if applicable
Register of Directors and officers, where maintained under applicable corporate records practice
Accounting books and annual accounts documentation

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 325-1,300 per year, depending on the city, mail handling, nominee or local representative services, and filing support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500-10,000 for a small Spanish SL, depending on turnover, transaction volume, group reporting, related-party activity, and audit complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Newly incorporated entities generally qualify for a 15% rate in the first profitable tax period and the immediately following period, subject to statutory conditions. Qualifying start-up companies may also apply a 15% rate during the applicable qualifying periods. Small-entity, cooperative, Canary Islands, and other sector-specific regimes may provide reduced rates or tax credits. Research, development, innovation, employment, audiovisual production, and certain investment activities may qualify for deductions. The general participation exemption may eliminate Spanish corporate tax on qualifying dividends and capital gains, normally subject to a 5% non-deductible expense adjustment and minimum holding requirements. Tax losses may be carried forward without a statutory time limit, but their annual utilization is subject to percentage limitations based on prior-year turnover, with a general minimum offset allowance of EUR 1 million.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited, subject to statutory annual utilization limitations and anti-abuse rules

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Corporate Income Tax and Non-Resident Income Tax return for permanent establishments, filed electronically through the Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT) electronic headquarters using an electronic certificate or other accepted identification method
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax year. For a calendar-year company ending on 31 December, the usual filing period is 1 to 25 July of the following year. If the final day is not a business day, the applicable electronic filing deadline is extended under the AEAT calendar rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Spanish tax identification number (NIF), registered office, tax period, entity type, activity classification, and filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder or parent must not be entered as the taxpayer where the Spanish SL is the taxable entity. Record the SL's Spanish NIF and identify the non-resident owner in related-party and withholding documentation where relevant.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit or loss reported in the statutory annual accounts before Spanish corporate tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use Spanish statutory accounts prepared under Spanish GAAP or the applicable accepted accounting framework. A foreign parent's consolidation figures are not a substitute for the SL's standalone accounting result.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs and deductions for non-deductible expenses, depreciation differences, provisions, impairment, financial expenses, exempt income, and other book-to-tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not deduct foreign parent costs unless the SL received identifiable services, the charge is arm's length, and the benefit and supporting evidence are documented. Apply Spanish interest limitation, anti-hybrid, anti-abuse, and transfer-pricing rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Use of prior-year Spanish tax losses, subject to annual percentage limits and the EUR 1 million minimum offset allowance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign group losses cannot generally be imported into the Spanish SL. Loss utilization may be denied or restricted in abusive acquisitions of loss-making companies or where the statutory ownership-change conditions are met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and deductions for qualifying R&D, technological innovation, employment, audiovisual productions, investments, donations, and other statutory incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain Spanish invoices, technical reports, payroll records, project descriptions, eligibility certificates, and payment evidence. Group-level economic ownership does not alone establish Spanish eligibility.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base after adjustments and loss utilization, multiplied by the applicable corporate income tax rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The ordinary SL rate is 25%. Apply the 15% new-entity or start-up rate only after verifying all statutory conditions and exclusions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Payments on account and withholding credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for Modelo 202 installments, Spanish withholding tax, and other permitted prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile every credit to AEAT payment records and withholding certificates. Foreign tax credits require separate statutory analysis and cannot be claimed solely because foreign tax was commercially incurred.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net corporate tax after installments, withholding credits, and applicable deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay electronically from an authorized Spanish or accepted European payment channel. Refund claims should be supported by bank details, accounting reconciliation, and evidence that the filing is final and internally approved.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of transactions with related entities, including services, royalties, loans, guarantees, cost allocations, and IP arrangements, where reporting thresholds apply.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the ultimate parent, group entities, transaction categories, amounts, pricing method, and documentation status. Data-labeling services, software access, management services, and financing from foreign affiliates require contemporaneous support.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing with tax payable generally triggers a surcharge of 1% plus an additional 1% for each complete month of delay during the first 12 months. After 12 months, the surcharge is generally 15%, plus late-payment interest from the end of that 12-month period. Voluntary late filing without tax payable may attract a fixed penalty, generally EUR 200, potentially reduced where legally available. Failure to file after a tax authority request may produce a minimum penalty of EUR 200 and percentage-based penalties. Deliberate tax underpayment may trigger penalties of 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, depending on the severity of the infringement, in addition to tax and interest.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202, Corporate Income Tax installment-payment declaration, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly, where the entity is subject to installment payments
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally 1 to 20 April, October, and December. The December installment is normally due from 1 to 20 December. Large companies subject to the alternative tax-base method may have additional calculation requirements. The final corporate tax liability is settled through Modelo 200.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Spanish NIF, legal name, tax period, and installment period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Spanish SL's NIF. The foreign shareholder is not the filer unless it independently has a Spanish taxable presence or filing obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation based either on the prior year's assessed corporate tax or, where mandatory or elected, the current-period accounting tax base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the method applicable to the entity's turnover and elections. Reconcile the calculation with management accounts and Modelo 200.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Installment due after applicable credits and prior payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not net unrelated foreign withholding taxes or foreign tax credits against the Spanish installment unless expressly permitted.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment or late filing may generate statutory surcharges, late-payment interest, and formal filing penalties. Incorrect installment calculations may be corrected in the annual return and can create interest and tax underpayment penalties. Repeated failure can increase audit and enforcement risk.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 232, Informative declaration of related-party transactions and transactions with jurisdictions classified as non-cooperative or low-tax jurisdictions, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally during the month following the ten-month period after the end of the tax period. For a 31 December year-end, the usual deadline is 30 November of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amounts and categories of transactions with related parties, including services, financing, royalties, asset transfers, and other controlled transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Aggregate and report transactions according to the applicable category and counterparty rules. Ensure consistency with the Local File, general ledger, invoices, agreements, and Modelo 200.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transactions requiring reporting under the applicable aggregate and category thresholds, including material transactions using the same valuation method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Review every foreign group payment and receipt, even where the amount is below the documentation threshold, because arm's-length and record-keeping obligations may still apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reportable transactions involving jurisdictions designated under Spanish legislation or applicable European and international lists.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm the counterparty's current jurisdiction status for the relevant tax year. A commercial label such as 'payment platform' does not eliminate beneficial-owner and jurisdiction analysis.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Incorrect or incomplete informative filings may lead to fixed or proportional penalties under the General Tax Law. Material misreporting may also support transfer-pricing adjustments and tax-evasion proceedings where unpaid tax exceeds criminal thresholds.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish withholding tax on dividends and other profit distributions to non-residents, subject to domestic exemptions and applicable tax treaties. Qualifying EU or EEA parent companies may obtain full exemption under the Spanish implementation of the Parent-Subsidiary Directive where ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, legal-form, and anti-abuse conditions are satisfied. A treaty may reduce the rate, commonly to 5%, 10%, or 15%, depending on the treaty and ownership percentage.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the beneficial owner issued by its tax authority and verify treaty residence, beneficial ownership, minimum holding, holding period, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose rules, and anti-abuse requirements. Apply the reduced rate only where Spanish procedural requirements permit source relief. Otherwise withhold 19% and allow the recipient to seek a refund from the AEAT using the applicable non-resident tax refund procedure. Retain the residence certificate, ownership chart, treaty analysis, board resolutions, payment records, and evidence of beneficial ownership. Report and pay withholding through Modelo 123 and provide the annual information return through Modelo 193.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The ordinary Spanish domestic withholding rate for Spanish-source interest and royalties paid to non-residents is generally 19%, subject to applicable exemptions and treaties. Interest and royalty payments to qualifying associated companies resident in another EU Member State, or in certain qualifying EEA jurisdictions, may be exempt under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive implementation where minimum ownership, beneficial-owner, subject-to-tax, holding-period, and anti-abuse conditions are met. Tax treaties commonly reduce royalty rates to approximately 5% to 10% and interest rates to approximately 0% to 10%, but the specific treaty must be checked. Spanish-source service fees are generally not subject to Spanish non-resident withholding solely because the payer is Spanish unless they constitute a Spanish permanent-establishment income category or another specifically taxable category.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File documentation is generally required for controlled transactions with the same related person or entity exceeding EUR 250,000 in the relevant transaction category during the tax period, subject to statutory exclusions and special rules. Master File documentation is generally required for Spanish entities forming part of a multinational group where consolidated group turnover is at least EUR 750 million. Country-by-country reporting generally applies at the EUR 750 million consolidated group-revenue threshold and is normally filed by the reporting entity in the relevant jurisdiction, with Spanish notification obligations where applicable.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not operate a separate UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime. Nevertheless, Spanish tax law requires genuine economic activity, arm's-length conduct, beneficial ownership, and business purpose. The tax authorities may apply the general anti-abuse rule, simulation doctrine, recharacterization, transfer-pricing rules, controlled-foreign-company rules, anti-hybrid rules, interest-limitation rules, principal-purpose tests, and EU anti-abuse principles. A Spanish SL performing data labeling or AI-training BPO should maintain Spanish personnel or demonstrable operational capacity, premises or documented remote-work infrastructure, decision-making evidence, customer contracts, time records, service deliverables, cybersecurity controls, and commercially rational pricing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing revenue, fabricating expenses, using false invoices, diverting customer receipts to foreign accounts, or deliberately underreporting Spanish taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties may generally range from 50% to 150% of unpaid tax, in addition to tax and interest. Where the amount defrauded exceeds EUR 120,000 for a tax period, the conduct may constitute a criminal tax offense punishable by imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and a fine of up to six times the amount defrauded. Aggravated cases, including amounts exceeding EUR 600,000 or organized fraud, may carry imprisonment of 2 to 6 years and higher fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may incur civil liability, subsidiary tax liability, administrative sanctions, and criminal liability where they participated in or knowingly enabled the conduct. Courts may impose asset seizure, disqualification, and travel restrictions where legally justified; travel bans are not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing or accepting invoices for non-existent data-labeling services, inflating intercompany service charges, claiming input VAT without genuine business activity, or misclassifying supplies to manipulate VAT or withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT assessments, repayment of improperly claimed input tax, late-payment interest, and administrative penalties generally calculated as a percentage of the improperly deducted or unpaid tax. Serious or organized conduct may constitute a tax or accounting crime under the Criminal Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve fictitious invoices or knowingly sign false tax returns may face joint civil restitution, subsidiary tax liability, criminal prosecution, asset seizure, professional disqualification, and imprisonment where criminal thresholds are met.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging foreign affiliates for unsubstantiated management services, royalties, financing, or data-processing services; applying loss-making terms without functional analysis; or omitting required Local File, Master File, or Modelo 232 information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AEAT may make a primary adjustment to arm's-length income, deny unsupported deductions, impose secondary adjustments, assess interest, and apply transfer-pricing documentation penalties. Failure to document or materially misreporting controlled transactions can generate fixed or transaction-linked penalties under Spanish tax law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability for tax losses caused by knowingly unsupported related-party arrangements and criminal exposure if the adjustment forms part of deliberate tax fraud exceeding the criminal threshold.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing dividends, interest, or royalties through an intermediary with no substantive activity, claiming treaty benefits without beneficial ownership, submitting an invalid tax-residence certificate, or using a conduit entity to obtain EU directive relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of exemption or treaty reduction, assessment of unpaid withholding tax, interest, and applicable penalties. Anti-abuse rules may recharacterize the arrangement and impose withholding at the domestic rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving knowingly false beneficial-owner representations may incur withholding-tax liability, civil restitution, administrative penalties, and criminal liability for document fraud or tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Spanish SL with nominee directors, no personnel or operational capability, no genuine customer or supplier activity, and using the company solely to receive funds, access treaty benefits, or shift profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AEAT may disregard artificial arrangements, deny deductions and exemptions, recharacterize transactions, impose tax and interest, and apply the general anti-abuse rule. Criminal consequences may arise if the structure facilitates tax fraud, money laundering, or falsification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners may face civil liability, tax-liability derivation, asset freezing, disqualification, and criminal prosecution. Corporate personality is not automatically disregarded, but veil piercing may occur in cases of fraud, abuse, commingling, or unlawful evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify customers or beneficial owners, accepting unexplained mass payouts, processing funds unrelated to the stated AI-data business, failing to retain records, or ignoring suspicious transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Spanish Law 10/2010, serious and very serious AML infringements may result in public or private reprimands, temporary suspension, and fines that can reach EUR 1.5 million, 5% of the net worth of the obligated person, or up to ten times the value of the transaction or benefit, subject to the applicable classification and statutory limits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers and directors may be personally sanctioned where the infringement is attributable to them. Criminal money-laundering liability may include imprisonment, fines, confiscation, and disqualification. Travel restrictions may be imposed by a court when necessary for criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining incomplete ledgers, omitting related-party balances, backdating invoices, failing to prepare or deposit annual accounts, or presenting accounts that materially conceal the company's financial position.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate, accounting, commercial-register, and tax consequences may include fines, refusal or delay of registry filings, administrative tax adjustments, audit qualifications, and criminal accounting liability where the conduct causes material deception or supports fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur liability for losses caused to the company, shareholders, creditors, or the tax authority, and may face disqualification, civil restitution, or criminal sanctions for deliberate falsification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Treating employees as contractors to avoid Spanish payroll taxes and social-security contributions, paying undeclared workers, or failing to withhold employment income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Back assessments, social-security contributions, surcharges, employment-tax interest, labor fines, and potentially criminal sanctions may apply. The exact amount depends on the period, number of workers, concealment, and severity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur subsidiary liability for unpaid social-security obligations and withholding taxes, civil claims from workers, labor sanctions, and criminal liability in aggravated cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Data Protection, Confidentiality, and AI-Training Misuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing personal data without a lawful basis, transferring labeled datasets outside the EEA without safeguards, using special-category data without appropriate controls, or breaching customer confidentiality and processor obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Spanish Data Protection Agency may impose GDPR administrative fines of up to EUR 20 million or 4% of worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher, for the relevant infringement category, in addition to corrective orders, processing bans, and contractual damages.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil and, in exceptional cases, criminal liability for unlawful disclosure, secrecy breaches, or intentional misuse. GDPR fines are generally imposed on the company, but individual liability may arise under separate civil or criminal provisions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating mass payout, remittance, stored-value, or payment-account services without the required authorization, or using PayPal or Wise accounts in a manner inconsistent with their terms and regulated-business restrictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory orders, account suspension, repayment obligations, administrative fines, and potential criminal consequences may apply depending on whether the conduct constitutes unauthorized payment services, fraud, or money laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for knowingly operating unauthorized financial services, misleading banks or payment institutions, or facilitating illicit funds. Asset seizure and travel restrictions may be ordered in criminal proceedings.
